silk.definition: A fabric made from the fine threads produced by certain insect larvae.
silk.exampleUsage: The composition record identifies the scarf as silk.

wool.definition: Soft hair from sheep, used to make warm cloth.

linen.definition: A fabric woven with fibers from the flax plant.

cashmere.definition: A soft fabric made from the wool of the Cashmere goat.

hemp.definition: A strong plant fiber used to make fabric, rope, and other products.

bamboo.definition: A textile description that may refer to directly processed bamboo fiber or, commonly, rayon made using bamboo as a cellulose source.

jute.definition: A strong plant fiber used to make coarse cloth, sacks, and rope.

mohair.definition: Fabric made with yarn made from the silky hair of the Angora goat.

alpaca.definition: A soft textile fiber obtained from alpacas, or fabric made from it.

polyester.definition: A synthetic fiber used to make fabrics and other products.

nylon.definition: A strong synthetic material used in clothing and other products.

acrylic.definition: A synthetic fabric made from polyacrylonitrile.

spandex.definition: An elastic synthetic fiber used in stretch fabrics.

rayon.definition: A manufactured fiber made from processed cellulose.

lycra.definition: A trademark used for elastane fibers, also called spandex.

microfiber.definition: Fabric made from very fine synthetic fibers.

gore-tex.definition: A brand of material used in products designed to be waterproof and breathable.

kevlar.definition: Describes materials made with Kevlar fibers or composites, valued for their high tensile strength and impact resistance in protective gear.

neoprene.definition: A synthetic rubber used in foam sheets and other materials, including some garments.

velvet.definition: A silky densely piled fabric with a plain back.

satin.definition: A weave that creates a smooth face, or fabric made with that weave using various fibers.

chiffon.definition: A lightweight sheer woven fabric made from silk or other fibers.

organza.definition: A crisp sheer woven fabric made from silk or other fibers.

brocade.definition: A rich fabric with raised patterns woven into it.

jacquard.definition: Fabric with a pattern woven into it using a special loom.

crepe.definition: A soft thin light fabric with a crinkled surface.

tulle.definition: A fine (often starched) net used for veils or tutus or gowns.

lace.definition: An open decorative textile made with threads forming patterned holes.

weave.definition: The pattern in which threads are interlaced to form fabric.

warp.definition: The lengthwise threads held tight during weaving.

weft.definition: The yarn woven across the warp yarn in weaving.

thread-count.definition: Thread count is a measure of the number of threads per square inch of fabric.

weight.definition: How heavy a fabric is for a given area.

drape.definition: The manner in which fabric hangs or falls.

stretch.definition: The ability of a fabric to extend when pulled.

breathability.definition: The ability of a fabric to allow air or moisture vapor to pass through.

durability.definition: The ability of fabric to resist wear or damage over time.

hand-wash.definition: To wash clothing by hand rather than in a machine.

machine-wash.definition: Clean clothing or fabric items using a washing machine.
machine-wash.exampleUsage: Can I machine-wash this garment, or does its care label require another method?

dry-clean.definition: Clean clothing with chemical solvents rather than water.

iron.definition: To smooth wrinkles in fabric with a heated iron.

steam.definition: To use steam to refresh fabric or remove wrinkles.

bleach.definition: To whiten fabric or remove color using a bleaching agent.

tumble-dry.definition: To dry laundry in a rotating dryer, with heat or unheated air depending on the setting.

line-dry.definition: To dry clothing by hanging it on a line.

stain-removal.definition: The process of removing unwanted marks from fabric.

fabric-softener.definition: A laundry product used to make washed fabric feel softer.
